Container.Name: Stackyard
Container.Overview: A self-hosted homelab dashboard you actually want to look at.[br][br]Most dashboards are a wall of numbers and charts. Stackyard is the opposite: a calm, launcher-style grid of app tiles, folders, and a small number of genuinely useful widgets. Built to be glanced at a hundred times a day without feeling cluttered.[br][br]Everything is set up from the browser. Add app tiles, group them into folders, arrange pages, and drop in widgets for the services you already run. Widgets cover Docker, system health, downloads, media, backups, network and more.[br][br]Runs as one container with no external database and no runtime dependencies. Configuration and uploaded icons persist in the two paths below.[br][br]Note: most homelab services live on private addresses. The Allow Private IPs setting below is on by default so links and widgets pointing at your other containers work. Turn it off to keep the SSRF guard enabled.

Container.DonateText: If Stackyard is useful to you, you can buy me a coffee.
Container.Changes:
### 1.19.0 - 2026-10-20
### Added
- Nine short Backup haikus that fit small cards.
- Let a widget manifest list the query parameters its data function reads.
- Settings offers to add the address you are signed in on to Allowed Addresses.
### Changed
- The Unsplash wallpaper changes once a day instead of on every load.
- Log a failing widget once, with a reminder every 10 minutes and a line on recovery, instead of on every request.
- Redraw the Weather widget artwork as frosted glass with gentle motion that pauses off screen.
- Choose the icon colour style (Dark, White, Auto, Clear or Color) from a drop-down; colours and sliders show only under Color.
- Badge and wallpaper colour swatches sit together at the end of their row, all one size.
### Fixed
- Name a widget without a manifest for re-entry when a port map change clears its settings.
- Backup cards show a whole haiku or none, never part of one.
- Show an error instead of zero DNS queries, "Nothing playing" or "Not secured" when a service sends an unreadable reply.
- Stop a large non-JSON reply from a service from stalling the dashboard.
- Show an error when a widget cannot draw the data it received, instead of leaving old data on screen.
- Keep healthy Backup cards when another backup server stops answering.
- Answer every widget request before the dashboard's proxy gives up, even when a service stalls on several calls.
- Keep the dashboard and healthy widgets responsive while several services stall.
- Keep every widget, badge and health check working while the DNS server is down, instead of stalling behind lookups that never finish.
- Keep app health dots updating while the Docker socket proxy stops answering.
- Treat a damaged settings block in the config file as damage instead of loading it as an open install.
- Skip invalid entries in the config file's app list instead of failing health checks, badges and widgets.
- Keep a config file edited by hand while the container runs instead of overwriting it on the next save.
- Report no changes when importing an export that matches the current configuration.
- Stop an icon upload from overwriting an existing icon when many share its name.
- The Referrer policy picker shows and selects Default.
- Now Playing no longer cuts off the second line of a long title.
- Stop extra query values on widget data requests from filling server memory and multiplying upstream calls.
- Stop app tiles with a refresh interval from filling the browser Back history.
- Stop the Connections VPN view from stacking animation loops while its page is off screen.
- Pause the Analog clock, Connections map and VPN animations on dashboard pages not shown.
- Adding or removing a row in a widget's settings keeps the stored passwords and keys of the other rows.
- Colour pickers in Settings fit on narrow phones without cutting off labels or swatches.
- Colour sliders in Settings share one length.
- Safari no longer logs a viewport warning when the dashboard loads.
### Security
- Keep a stored widget secret out of the browser when a save sends the widget under a legacy type.
- Withhold stored secrets when a widget's type changes, the port map is removed, or certificate checking for widgets is turned on or off.
- Stop trusting the first host name that opens Stackyard while no password is set. Add a domain name in Allowed Addresses from an IP address or a local name.
- Refuse service names that resolve to loopback or link-local addresses, such as `ip6-localhost`, in admin URL tests.
- Block 6to4, local-use NAT64 and site-local IPv6 addresses in admin URL tests.
- Refuse a config save whose settings block is not an object, which could remove the password.
- Refuse a config save or import nested too deeply, which could leave the config unreadable.
- Saving the wallpaper no longer replaces the stored Unsplash key with the field's label.
- Icons always load through the server, so the CDN does not learn which services a dashboard shows.
- A page on another site can no longer lock the owner out of sign-in by pointing its host name at the server.
- The wallpaper endpoint no longer returns Unsplash's error text.
- A session cookie set by another host on the same parent domain no longer signs the owner out.
- The Connections widget no longer names an address the guard blocked.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port the dashboard is reached on.

Config.Name: Config Storage
Config.Description: Dashboard configuration. Keep this, or every setting is lost on update.

Config.Name: Icon Storage
Config.Description: Icons you upload for your app tiles.

Config.Name: Allow Private IPs
Config.Description: Let widgets and badges reach private addresses, which most homelab services use. Set to false to keep the SSRF guard on.

Config.Name: Docker Socket Proxy URL
Config.Description: Optional. Address of a Docker socket proxy, for the Docker widgets. Example: http://socket-proxy:2375

Config.Name: Trust Proxy
Config.Description: Optional. Set to true when running behind a reverse proxy, so client addresses are read from the forwarded headers.

Config.Name: Node Options
Config.Description: Node heap cap. Keep it near half the --memory limit in Extra Parameters, and raise both together.
